best_for: Windows users who need more than Microsoft Paint for photo touch-ups and simple graphics, with layers and effects, but do not want Photoshop's price or learning curve.
description:
paint.net is a photo and image editor for Windows from dotPDN LLC. It began as a college senior design project mentored by Microsoft, meant as a free step up from Microsoft Paint, and Rick Brewster now develops and maintains it.

Each open image gets its own tab with a live thumbnail, so you can hop between pictures fast. You can draw with pressure-sensitive pens from Wacom, UGEE, Microsoft and others. It opens and saves PNG, JPEG, JPEG XL, AVIF, HEIC, WebP, TIFF and more. Built-in fixes include red-eye removal, sharpening, curves and levels, plus a 3D Rotate/Zoom effect for adding tilt and perspective. Color management keeps photos with embedded color profiles looking as the camera captured them.

points.title: Layers, effects and unlimited undo
points.text: paint.net adds layers, unlimited undo, a set of effects and adjustments, and the usual selection and drawing tools. It sits between Microsoft Paint and full photo editors.

points.title: Free download, paid Store copy
points.text: The classic download from the official site is free. The Microsoft Store version costs money, has the same features and updates itself, so buying it is a way to support the developer.

points.title: Fine for work use
points.text: The license allows use at home, in business and in government at no charge. It is freeware, not open source: you may not modify, resell or redistribute changed copies.

points.title: Windows only, and a modern PC
points.text: There is no Mac or Linux version. It needs Windows 10 21H2 or newer, Windows 11 or Server 2022, a 64-bit CPU with at least 4 cores (x64 with AVX2, or Arm64), and Direct3D 11 graphics.

points.title: Plugins fill the gaps
points.text: Extra effects and file types come from community plugins shared on the official forum. The license says plugins may not be passed on without their author's permission, so get them from the forum.

points.title: Two versions to fall back on
points.text: The listing here has x64 and Arm64 builds and keeps 2 versions, including the current 5.2.
